history.sg_progress: The Office of Information and Communications Technology has completed a comprehensive review of its core services and associated costs, with the primary objectives of: (a) determining the cost of services provided to other United Nations Secretariat entities; (b) establishing a transparent pricing model for each service; and (c) updating service rates. This exercise has resulted in a more accurate and sustainable financial framework that reflects current operational realities and is aligned with best practices as outlined in the cost-recovery policy and guidelines. Three core service rates were approved by the Controller: (a) the United Nations Headquarters core services bundle at $1,156 per user; (b) the peacekeeping core rate at $667 per user; and (c) the non-headquarters/non-field core bundle at $320 per user, applicable to offices away from Headquarters, economic commissions and similar entities. In addition, a rate of $62 for IP telephony services for New York-based users was approved in February 2025. Legacy rates for other on-demand services remain in effect until the newly proposed rates are formally approved.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration ensure that the Office of Information and Communications Technology expedites the new review of the full category of services and continues to enhance oversight to match revenue against expenses at the service or functional level, as appropriate, to ensure that the full cost of each category can be measured realistically and objectively.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Office of Information and Communications Technology has undertaken a structured and data-driven review of its services, costs and cost-recovery methodology in consultation with the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget. Service bundles based on the distinct needs and usage patterns of different user populations, namely United Nations Headquarters, field missions and others (non-field/away from Headquarters), have been developed. The approved rates for these service bundles have been operationalized with the set-up of the activity codes in Umoja to allow the Office of Information and Communications Technology to exercise cost recovery. The pricing model took into account the distinction between regular budget and support account assessed resources, allowing identification of the remaining funding gap to be addressed through cost recovery revenue. Additionally, the pricing model was designed to capture the underlying cost elements of ICT function under each service provider. Following the development and approval of ICT service rates in coordination with the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget, an annual update of these rates will be performed to ensure alignment with evolving operational requirements and costs. This process will be supported by continuous monitoring of service consumption patterns, client base dynamics, underlying costs and cost recovery performance, including uncollected revenue. These insights will inform future rate revisions and help the financial sustainability of the Office.
history.board_assessment: Given that the new ICT service rates, developed and approved in coordination with the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget, are in place, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
